vulnerablePoints.title: Pigeon Island
vulnerablePoints.detail: Weather, rough sea, or a slow ticket queue could eat into its morning-into-midday window on Day 1. It's the one activity that can't easily be moved later (crowds and wind both increase through the afternoon).

vulnerablePoints.title: Koneswaram Temple
vulnerablePoints.detail: Its 1:00–4:00 PM midday closure and 6:45 PM hard close, combined with the fixed 6:00 PM Verandas target, create the tightest window on Day 1. Lunch is deliberately unhurried specifically to avoid arriving at the temple before it reopens.

vulnerablePoints.title: Kanniya Hot Springs
vulnerablePoints.detail: Reports of long queues for the bathing baskets; the plan treats it as a quick visit specifically to avoid this risk.

vulnerablePoints.title: Group size itself
vulnerablePoints.detail: Every stop has a "get 16 people off/on the bus" tax; delays compound across the day rather than staying isolated.

vulnerablePoints.title: Afternoon kayaking at Kantale
vulnerablePoints.detail: Runs outside its ideal cool-morning-calm-water slot to fit the drive home. If Marble Beach or lunch overruns, this is the activity with the least slack behind it before sunset (~6:14–6:21 PM) — watch the 4:55 PM departure-from-Kantale time closely.

vulnerablePoints.title: No dedicated rest block on Day 2
vulnerablePoints.detail: The extended Pigeon Island block on Day 1 and the beach/lunch stops on Day 2 are the main breathing room before the long overnight drive; if the group is visibly fatigued, that's the first place to add time back, not cut it.

vulnerablePoints.title: Return journey
vulnerablePoints.detail: Driver fatigue and night driving after two long days is the single biggest safety factor. The final leg has ~1 hour of slack built in above the realistic driving time to protect against this.

contingencySteps: Day 1 — first cut: shorten the Nilaveli dry-off/relax block (12:40–1:10 PM) rather than cut into Pigeon Island itself — it's the trip's highest-value activity.
Day 1 — second cut: shorten lunch back toward 60 min (it currently carries 20 min of slack built in for the Koneswaram midday closure).

Day 1 — protect Koneswaram Temple and the 6:00 PM Verandas arrival above the above two — reorder if needed so the group reaches the temple with enough time left before its 6:45 PM close, even if that means a slightly later arrival at the accommodation.
Day 2 — first cut: shorten or skip Kanniya Hot Springs (lowest cost to the overall experience).
Day 2 — second cut: shorten Marble Beach to 45–60 min rather than 90.
Day 2 — if still behind, shorten kayaking back toward 90–100 min rather than push the Habarana/Dambulla dinner past dark.
Day 2 — protect the ~7:20 PM departure from Habarana/Dambulla above everything else — the return leg's built-in slack is designed to be trimmed first if the day is running behind.
